F-02 / Approach
Approach

From data
to conviction.

Our method fits in one sentence: measure before you believe. Every opportunity goes through five stages and a proprietary six-factor model before reaching the investment committee.

Selection rate
< 1%
Model factors
6
Data sources
38
Average review
14 weeks
01 Process

Five stages,
one standard.

The process is the same for every strategy. Only the model weightings and the type of instrument change.

Stage 01/05

Sourcing

1,200opportunities analysed
01 — Sourcing

A proprietary flow, qualified continuously.

A proprietary network of federations, leagues, clubs, broadcasters, agents and investment banks. Every opportunity is logged, qualified and tracked in our systems — even when declined.

  • Continuous coverage of twelve sports
  • Qualification within ten business days
  • Full history kept for every opportunity
02 — Modelling

A model that forces you to be explicit.

Shortlisted opportunities enter the Freya model: six factors weighted by strategy, calibrated on historical transactions and sporting performance.

  • Multi-factor score out of 100
  • Sporting performance scenarios
  • Sensitivity to rights cycles
03 — Due diligence

Four diligences, two sets of eyes.

Financial, legal, sporting, reputational: each dimension is investigated by a pair, then cross-checked by an independent third party.

  • Review of rights and sponsorship contracts
  • Audit of wage bill and transfers
  • Field interviews: staff, athletes, partners
04 — Committee

A written decision, and a challenged one.

Written memorandum, adversarial review, unanimous decision. For every case, one partner is appointed to argue the opposite position.

  • Standardised memorandum
  • Appointed devil’s advocate
  • Reasoned, archived decision
05 — Investment

A thesis reviewed every year.

Instrument structuring, a 100-day plan, governance, Advisory support. Monitoring is monthly; the thesis is reviewed every year, without complacency.

  • 100-day plan
  • Board seat or observer
  • Annual thesis review
02 The Freya model

Six factors,
one score out of 100.

The model compares each asset with the median of its universe. It does not decide: it forces us to state what we believe, and why.

Freya score — example
73/100

Universe median: 52. Committee threshold: 65.

  • Sporting performance20%

    Results, progression, squad depth, tracking data.

  • Audience20%

    Attendance, TV and streaming audiences, digital communities.

  • Revenue20%

    Quality, recurrence and diversification of revenue.

  • Governance15%

    Board independence, cost control, compliance.

  • Rights & assets15%

    Media and sponsorship contracts, real estate, academy, brand.

  • Impact10%

    Equality, local roots, environmental footprint.

03 Risk management

Name the risks
before they happen.

Six risk families are mapped for every holding and reviewed by a committee chaired independently of management.

Fig. 03

Risk map — probability and impact (1 to 5)

RiskMitigationReview
R1SportingRelegation, injuries, lasting underperformance.Relegation clauses, diversification across sports, insurance cover.Monthly
R2Media rightsDownward renegotiation of broadcast contracts.Maturities aligned with rights cycles, stress scenarios.Quarterly
R3CounterpartyDefault of a broadcaster, sponsor or debtor club.Rated counterparties, enforceable security, group limits.Monthly
R4RegulatoryChanges to league and federation financial rules.Legal monitoring, dialogue with governing bodies, adaptation clauses.Quarterly
R5ReputationGovernance or conduct contrary to our principles.Reputational due diligence, ethics clauses, exit rights.Ongoing
R6LiquidityDifficulty exiting a minority stake.Long horizon, tag-along rights, shareholder agreements.Half-yearly
